tests.title: The webhook secret is generated once or supplied
given: an active workspace with no webhook secret
a service with an external URL and one without
tests.when: the webhook route is called with no body, with an empty object, with a null secret, and with a supplied 32-character secret, and the workspace's secrets and the description route are then read
then: the three generating calls answer 200 with configured true and a 64-character lowercase hex secret
the supplied-secret call answers 200 with no secret field and stores the value supplied
the URL is the ingress address, or null where the service has no external URL
the generated secret appears in no later response, log record, event or delivery row
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook routes' integration test file: r = put(webhook); assert len(r.json.secret) == 64; assert 'secret' not in get(forge).json.webhook

tests.title: A malformed or disallowed secret is refused
given: an active workspace, an archived one, and a workspace holding 100 secrets
tests.when: the webhook route is called with a non-object body, a non-string secret, secrets of 15 and 256 characters, a secret containing a space and one containing a control character, against the full workspace, and against the archived workspace
then: each answers 400
each message names the rule broken and does not contain the value
the workspace's stored secret is unchanged in every case
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook routes' test file, table over the refused bodies asserting 400, the message and the stored secret

tests.title: Removing the secret closes the ingress and keeps the log
given: a workspace with a secret and two recorded deliveries, and an archived workspace with a secret
tests.when: the webhook route's removal is called for each, then called again, and a delivery is posted afterwards
then: each removal answers 204, including the repeat and the archived workspace
the recorded deliveries are still listed
a delivery posted afterwards answers 404
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook routes' integration test file: delete(webhook); assert delete(webhook).status == 204 and len(get(deliveries).json) == 2 and post(ingress).status == 404

tests.title: The secret is an ordinary workspace secret and is read afresh
given: a workspace, and the same secret name at the owner's user scope and the organization scope
tests.when: the secret is set through the secrets routes, a delivery is signed with it, it is rotated through the secrets routes, and a delivery is signed with the old and then the new value
then: the secret set through the secrets routes is accepted by the ingress
after the rotation the old value is refused and the new one accepted, with no restart
the user-scoped and organization-scoped secrets of the same name are never used
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook ingress integration test file: set_secret_via_secrets_route(v1); assert post(ingress, sign(v1)).status == 202; rotate(v2); assert post(ingress, sign(v1)).status == 401

tests.title: The delivery log lists what arrived, newest first, without the payload
given: a workspace with deliveries of each outcome, two recorded within one second, and a distinctive string in one payload
tests.when: the delivery log is read
then: the rows are newest first with the same-second pair ordered by recording time, latest first
every row carries the delivery id, forge, event, action, target, outcome, relayed events and received time
relayed is empty for every outcome but relayed
no row contains the distinctive payload string
tests.pseudocode: in the delivery log integration test file: r = get(deliveries); assert [x.received_at for x in r.json] == sorted(..., reverse=True) and SENTINEL not in r.text

tests.title: Bad delivery-log parameters are refused and the defaults applied
given: a workspace with 40 deliveries
tests.when: the log is read with no parameters, with a limit of 0, 101 and abc, with a malformed time bound, with a fractional time bound, and with each parameter given twice
then: the default limit is 30
the bad limits and the malformed time answer 400 naming the parameter
a repeated parameter answers 400 saying it must be given once
a fractional time bound starts at the next whole second
tests.pseudocode: in the delivery log test file, table over the parameter cases asserting the status and the returned count

tests.title: Deliveries are pruned after seven days and with their workspace
given: deliveries aged 6 days, exactly 7 days and one second, and 30 days, and deliveries of a workspace that has since been deleted
a controllable clock
tests.when: the hourly prune runs
then: the 7-day-and-one-second and 30-day deliveries are gone
the 6-day delivery remains
the deleted workspace's deliveries are gone whatever their age
tests.pseudocode: in the delivery log integration test file: run_prune(); assert ages_remaining() == [6] and deliveries_of(deletedWs) == []

tests.title: The ingress checks in order and reads the body last
given: a recording body reader, and combinations where two checks would both fail: an unknown slug with no signature header, a workspace without a secret with an oversized body, and a wrong GitLab token with an oversized body
tests.when: each combination is posted
then: each answers the refusal belonging to the earlier check
the body is not read for the unknown slug, the secretless workspace or the wrong GitLab token
the signature is verified only after the body has been read
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook ingress test file, table over the combinations asserting the status and bodyReader.calls == 0

tests.title: An unknown workspace and one without a secret are indistinguishable
given: a slug naming nothing, a workspace with no secret, a workspace with an empty secret, an archived workspace with a secret, and a secrets store made to raise
tests.when: a delivery is posted to each
then: the first three answer 404 with the same body
the archived workspace with a secret is processed normally
the failing store answers 500
no body is read for the 404s
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook ingress test file: assert resp(unknown) == resp(noSecret) == resp(emptySecret) and status == 404

tests.title: A missing, malformed or wrong signature is refused identically
given: a workspace with a known secret
tests.when: deliveries are posted with neither signature header, with a GitHub signature that is empty, malformed, of the wrong length and computed under another secret, with a GitLab token that is empty and wrong, and with a header given twice
then: each answers 401 with the same body
no delivery row is written and no event is emitted for any of them
the comparisons do not short-circuit on the first differing byte
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook ingress test file, table over the cases asserting 401, an unchanged log and no events

tests.title: GitHub's signature is verified over the raw bytes
given: a workspace with a known secret and a payload whose re-serialisation differs from the bytes sent, by key order and by whitespace
tests.when: a delivery is posted signed over the bytes as sent, and another signed over the re-serialised form
then: the signature over the bytes as sent is accepted
the signature over the re-serialised form is refused 401
the expected form is the sha256 prefix with 64 lowercase hex digits
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook ingress integration test file: assert post(raw, sign(raw)).status == 202 and post(raw, sign(reserialised)).status == 401

tests.title: An oversized body and a bad delivery identity are refused
given: a workspace with a secret
tests.when: deliveries are posted of exactly 1048576 and of 1048577 bytes, and with no delivery id, no event name, an id of 256 characters and an id containing a control character
then: the body at the limit is accepted and the one over it answers 413 body_too_large
each bad identity answers 400
no delivery row is written and no event emitted for any refusal
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook ingress test file, two tables asserting the statuses and an unchanged log

tests.title: A delivery is recorded before relaying and processed exactly once
given: a workspace with a secret and a delivery that maps to two events
tests.when: the delivery is posted, then posted again with the same id, then five copies are posted at the same time, and the same id is posted for a second workspace
then: the row exists before the first event is emitted
the repeat answers 202 duplicate, emitting nothing and adding no row
exactly one set of events is relayed for the five simultaneous copies
the same id for the other workspace is processed as its own delivery
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook ingress integration test file: post(d); assert post(d).json.outcome == 'duplicate'; post_concurrently(d, 5); assert events_for(d) == 2

tests.title: A failure to record refuses the delivery so it is redelivered
given: a delivery store made to raise on the insert
tests.when: a valid signed delivery is posted, the store is repaired, and the same delivery is posted again
then: the first answers 500 and emits no event
the second is processed in full rather than treated as a duplicate
its events are relayed
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook ingress test file: with store raising assert post(d).status == 500 and events == 0; repair(); assert post(d).json.outcome == 'relayed'

tests.title: The forge is answered before the events are relayed
given: an event recorder made to block, and a forge client that disconnects as soon as it is answered
tests.when: a valid delivery is posted
then: the 202 is written before the first event is emitted
the forge's connection is not held open by the recorder
the events are still relayed after the forge has disconnected
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook ingress integration test file: r = post(d); assert r.received_at < firstEvent.emitted_at; disconnect(); assert eventually(events_for(d) == expected)

tests.title: Each outcome is reported in the answer and the log
given: deliveries that map to events, that map to none, that are about another repository, and one already recorded
tests.when: each is posted
then: the outcomes are relayed, ignored, repository_mismatch and duplicate respectively
each outcome appears in the answer and in the delivery log row
the ignored and mismatched deliveries emit no event
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook ingress integration test file, table over the four deliveries asserting the outcome and the emitted events

tests.title: A payload missing what the delivery is about is recorded as malformed
given: bodies that are not one JSON object, and bodies missing the repository, the issue number, the label name and the push ref
a body missing only a title, a URL and a branch name
tests.when: each is posted with a valid signature
then: each of the first set answers 400 and is recorded with the outcome malformed
the body missing only descriptive fields is processed, with those fields defaulting to empty
no event is emitted for a malformed delivery
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook ingress integration test file, table over the bodies asserting the status, the recorded outcome and the emitted events

tests.title: The target is decided by comparing the repository path
given: a carry_patch workspace with an origin and an upstream, and a standard workspace
tests.when: deliveries are posted naming the origin's path, the upstream's path, each in a different case, and an unrelated path
then: a match with the origin is target origin
a match only with the upstream is target upstream
the comparison ignores case
an unrelated path is the repository_mismatch outcome with a null target
a standard workspace never reports target upstream
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook ingress integration test file, table over (payloadPath, workspaceKind, expectedTarget, expectedOutcome)

tests.title: The mapping tables are reproduced exactly
given: one delivery for every row of the GitHub and GitLab mapping tables, plus a ping, a GitHub pull_request labeled, an edited issue comment, a GitLab confidential hook and a note on a commit
a GitLab update removing three labels and adding two, and one changing 150 labels
tests.when: each is posted
then: each mapped delivery emits exactly the listed events with the listed metadata keys
a GitLab update emits its unlabeled events before its labeled ones, each group sorted by name
the 150-label update relays at most 100 label events and lists at most 100 labels in an event
each unmapped delivery relays nothing and reports the outcome ignored
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook mapping integration test file, driven from a table transcribed from the reference: post(d); assert [e.event_type for e in emitted()] == expected

tests.title: The payload is never kept and the forge is never called
given: a payload carrying a distinctive string in a field no mapping table lists
a recording log sink and a recording outbound client
tests.when: deliveries of every outcome are posted
then: no delivery row, log record or event metadata contains the distinctive string
no outbound request is made to the forge while processing any of them
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook ingress test file: post(d); assert SENTINEL not in (log.text + json(deliveries) + json(events)) and outbound.requests == 0

tests.title: A webhook is set up and its first delivery is relayed, against a running deployment
given: a running deployment, a workspace, and a client watching the event stream
tests.when: afc forge webhook set is run, a signed delivery about a labelled issue is posted to the printed URL, and the stream, the audit query and afc forge deliveries are read
then: the set prints a generated secret and the URL once
the delivery answers 202 with the outcome relayed
the labelled event reaches the stream and the audit query
the delivery log shows one row naming the relayed event
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook smoke test file: r = run('afc forge webhook set'); post(url, sign(secret, payload)); assert stream.next_event().event_type == 'hub.forge.issue.labeled'

tests.title: A redelivery changes nothing against a running deployment
given: a running deployment and a delivery already processed
tests.when: the same delivery id is posted again and the delivery log and the audit query are read
then: the repeat answers 202 with the outcome duplicate
no new event appears in the audit query
the delivery log still shows one row for that id
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook smoke test file: assert post(ingress, same).json.outcome == 'duplicate' and count_rows(id) == 1

tests.title: Unsigned and wrongly signed deliveries are refused against a running deployment
given: a running deployment and a workspace with a webhook secret
tests.when: a delivery is posted with no signature header and another with a signature computed under the wrong secret
then: each answers 401
the delivery log shows no row for either
the audit query shows no event for either
tests.pseudocode: in the webhook smoke test file: assert post(ingress, unsigned).status == 401 and post(ingress, badsig).status == 401 and get(deliveries).json == []
